comment: The reviewed map for scripts/codemods/semantic-colours.ts (WS01 step 23: ink and grounds). Every class it writes gives exactly the colour of the class it replaces on the plain :root, so with newLook off nothing changes; test/unit/semantic-map.test.ts proves it and holds the TSX files to this map. Not in this map: text-white on navy grounds (it stays), text-lca-gold (step 25), the grey and slate classes, the status colours and raw hex colours (step 24), border-lca-navy and ring-lca-navy, and the GOLD_BUTTON string in src/lib/brand.ts, which is not a TSX file. Navy tints keep the brand navy for now (see the navy-tint rule). Club colours are user data and stay inline styles. The judgement calls behind the sites and keep entries are recorded under step 23 in REDESIGN_STATUS.md.

rules.reason: Navy text on an opaque gold fill: the gold button and its copies, gold badges, the gold banners. The brief keeps navy text on gold in every look, and text-ink would be #e8ecf4 on gold in dark mode (about 1.9:1), so the text takes the navy that stays #1a2744 everywhere.
Navy text on the page, on a card or on a light tint: it follows the ink of the look, navy in light mode and #e8ecf4 in dark.
A white ground for page chrome or a control: it follows the surface of the look, #fff in light mode and #111a2c in dark.
A navy band, hero, card header, selected control, step number or badge: it stays #1a2744 in every look and in dark mode, so the white and gold on it keep their contrast.
The hover of a navy button (hover:bg-lca-navy/90): it stays with the navy fill it belongs to.

A navy tint keeps the brand navy at the same opacity: the faint tints behind a chip, an avatar, a selected row, a message or a note, the veil over the hero photo under white text, and the Exit button's hover on the gold banner. For a browser that cannot mix colours, such as Safari 15.4 to 16.1, Tailwind gives a brand colour with an opacity modifier its worked-out tint but a token utility only the token at full strength, so an ink tint would show there as a solid navy box behind navy text. In dark mode a navy tint barely shows on the dark ground; moving the tints to the ink, with a fallback of their own, is step 24's, with the navy borders beside them.

sites.reason: The trophy icon on the gold square of the membership band: the gold is on the parent element, so the navy-on-gold rule cannot see it.
The remove button over a page photo. Its icon is text-foreground, which turns light in dark mode, so its ground follows the surface instead of staying white.
The same remove button's hover, which goes with its ground.

keep.reason: A translucent white veil (bg-white/5 to bg-white/60, and their hover forms) on a navy ground or the dark hero photo. The ground stays navy or dark in every look, so the veil stays white, like text-white on it.

keep.contains: aspect-square w-full items-center justify-center overflow-hidden rounded-lg bg-white
keep.reason: The white mat behind a club logo on the clubs list. Logos are drawn for a white ground and are never recoloured, so the mat stays white in dark mode.
The white mat behind the club logo in the club page hero, which stays white for the same reason.
The white mat behind the club logo preview on the club's admin page, which shows the logo as visitors see it.
The white mat behind a club logo in the workspace list, which stays white for the same reason.

keep.contains: mx-auto w-fit rounded-lg border bg-white p-3
keep.reason: The white quiet zone around the two-step sign-in QR code. A phone camera reads dark modules on white, so it stays white in dark mode.
